The Myth Behind Defensive Gun Ownership

The fact of the matter is that any study put forth by either the Anti-gun or Pro-gun groups are heavily biased to support their point of view. In essence, these studies that use extrapolated data mean exactly nothing. The bulk of these studies are completely dependent on people not going and ascertaining the data for themselves. Lets take, for example, the concluding paragraph of this article...

"But the evidence clearly shows that our lax gun laws and increased gun ownership, spurred on by this myth, do not help “good guys with guns” defend themselves, their families or our society. Instead, they are aiding and abetting criminals by providing them with more guns, with 200,000 already stolen on an annual basis. And more guns means more homicides. More suicides. More dead men, women and children. Not fewer."

This statement is in direct contradiction with the FBI's Uniform Crime Report. Violent crimes are declining, not inclining. Is there a reference to this hard data anywhere in that article? No, but the article does open up with three cherry-picked incidents where people lost their lives at the hands of very stupid people. My point is, this is not a data-driven argument. The argument put forth by this article is driven by emotion, and as such, should be discarded by the intelligentsia.

(edited for grammar)

One of the studies put forth in this article has a sample size of 5800, focused on California (which has restrictive gun laws, by the way). That's not enough data to predict your way out of a wet paper bag, so we can discard the possibility of spotting a national crime trend. Another one of the studies doesn't even talk about sample size. So we can discard that right off the bat. Yes, folks, sample size really does matter!

In conclusion, bring me data to back up your point, not some type of feel-good hand-wringing campaign based on skewed studies, misinterpreted data, and erroneous conclusions.

Thomas Piketty Refuted Once and For All?

Link to the paper: http://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2543012

Challenging the Empirical Contribution of Thomas Piketty's Capital in the 21st Century

Phillip W. Magness

Robert P. Murphy

Abstract: "Thomas Piketty's Capital in the 21st Century has been widely debated on theoretical grounds, yet continues to attract acclaim for its historically-infused data analysis. In this study we conduct a closer scrutiny of Piketty's empirics than has appeared thus far, focusing upon his treatment of the United States. We find evidence of pervasive errors of historical fact, opaque methodological choices, and the cherry-picking of sources to construct favorable patterns from ambiguous data. Additional evidence suggests that Piketty used a highly distortive data assumption from the Soviet Union to accentuate one of his main historical claims about global “capitalism” in the 20th century. Taken together, these problems suggest that Piketty’s highly praised and historically-driven empirical work may actually be the book’s greatest weakness."
